title: Subcellular Fractionation of Suspension Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) Cells
author: Saumel Perez Rodriguez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf9sjr6e
materials: Discard supernatant gently to avoid any cell lost.

steps.title: Prepare Cell Culture
steps.instruction: Quantify cell concentration and viability during cell culture to reach 300-700 million viable cells with viability > 90%.

steps.title: Wash Cells
steps.instruction: Wash the cells twice using phosphate buffer (137 mM NaCl, 2.7 mM KCl, 8.1 mM Na2HPO4, 1.8 mM KH2PO4).

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge cells at 185 x g, 4 °C, for 5 minutes in 50 mL conical tubes.
Resuspend cellular pellet to approximately 3-7 x 10^7 cells/ml in 10 mL of cold phosphate buffer.
Repeat the centrifugation and resuspension steps once more.

steps.title: Swell Cells in Hypotonic Buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the cell pellet in 8 mL of hypotonic buffer (10 mM HEPES, 1 mM EDTA, pH 7.4).

substeps.instruction: Incubate the suspension on ice for 30 minutes, inverting the tube every 10 minutes.

steps.title: Add Inhibitors
steps.instruction: Add PMSF to a final concentration of 1 mM and 500 µL of prepared Protease Inhibitor Tablets for every 350 million cells.

substeps.instruction: To prepare Protease Inhibitor Tablets: dissolve one tablet in 100 mL sterile MilliQ water, filter through a 0.2 µm filter, distribute in 1 mL aliquots in 1-2 mL eppendorf tubes, and store at -20 °C.

steps.title: Disrupt Cells
steps.instruction: Disrupt cells using a Dounce homogenizer (or alternative methods like nitrogen cavitation, sonication, or Balch homogenizer).

substeps.instruction: Transfer cells to a Dounce homogenizer and perform 25 strokes on ice (optimize stroke number per cell line).
Immediately restore isotonicity by adding 2 mL of 45% (w/v) sucrose solution (prepared in hypotonic buffer) to the homogenate.

steps.title: Homogenize and Aliquot
steps.instruction: Transfer disrupted cells back to 50 mL tubes and homogenize by inversion, then distribute the homogenate into 1 mL aliquots in 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.

steps.title: Isolate Nuclear Fraction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge aliquots at 3000 x g, 4 °C, for 10 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Collect supernatant and transfer to new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes.
Tag the pellet as 'Nuclear Fraction' and maintain on ice.

steps.title: Isolate Mitochondrial Fraction
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the collected supernatant from the previous step at 9000 x g, 4 °C, for 10 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Collect and pool the new supernatant in 13.2 mL Open-Top Thinwall Ultra-Clear/Polypropylene Tubes (14 x 89 mm).
Tag the pellet as 'Mitochondrial Fraction' and maintain on ice.

steps.title: Isolate Microsomal Fraction and Cytosol
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the pooled supernatant at 100,000 x g, 4 °C, for 1 hour in a SW40Ti rotor (e.g., Optima XE-90 Ultracentrifuge).

substeps.instruction: Collect the supernatant in 15 mL conical tubes and tag as 'Cytosol'.
Tag the pellet as 'Microsomal Fraction'.
Maintain both on ice.

steps.title: Prepare Sucrose Gradients
steps.instruction: Prepare discontinuous sucrose gradients on ice in 13.2 mL Open-Top Thinwall Ultra-Clear/Polypropylene Tubes (14 x 89 mm) using a buffer of 10 mM HEPES and 1 mM EDTA, pH 7.4.

substeps.instruction: For Nuclear and Mitochondrial pellets: Deposit 1 mL 60% (w/v) sucrose at the bottom, followed by 3 mL each of 55%, 40%, and 30% (w/v) sucrose.
For Microsomal pellet: Deposit 1 mL 60% (w/v) sucrose at the bottom, followed by 2.5 mL each of 45%, 35%, 30%, and 10% (w/v) sucrose.
Ensure solutions are deposited in decreasing order of concentration and interfaces are clearly visible.

steps.title: Resuspend Pellets for Gradient
steps.instruction: Resuspend pellets in isotonic buffer [0.25 M sucrose, 10 mM HEPES, 1 mM EDTA, pH 7.4].

substeps.instruction: Mitochondrial pellets: Pool and resuspend gently in 1 mL isotonic buffer.
Nuclear pellets: Divide into 4 groups, pool each group, and resuspend gently in 1 mL isotonic buffer.
Microsomal pellet: Resuspend in 0.5 mL isotonic buffer.

steps.title: Separate Organelles via Ultracentrifugation
steps.instruction: Add each resuspended pellet to the top of its corresponding sucrose gradient and centrifuge at 217,874 x g, 4 °C, for 3 hours (max) in a SW40Ti rotor (Optima XE-90), using maximal acceleration and medium deceleration.

substeps.instruction: Collect visible bands using a Pasteur pipette, 1 mL micropipette tips, or peristaltic pump.
Note: 3 bands should be visible for most; 4 for nuclear. Discard the densest band at the bottom of the nuclear gradient as cell debris.

steps.title: Protein Precipitation
steps.instruction: Precipitate proteins from the cytosol or collected gradient fractions.

substeps.instruction: Add 260 µL of 4 M NaCl to 10 mL of sample in 50 mL conical tubes and homogenize by vortex.
Add 40 mL of cold 80% (v/v) acetone (pre-chilled at -20 °C for 16 hours) and homogenize by vortex or inversion.
Incubate at -20 °C for 16 hours.
Centrifuge at 8,228 x g, 4 °C, for 30 minutes and discard supernatant.
Wash the pellet by adding 40 mL of 80% (v/v) acetone, homogenizing, and centrifuging again at 8,228 x g, 4 °C, for 30 minutes; discard supernatant.
Repeat the wash step (Step 34-35) once more.
Centrifuge at 8,228 x g, 4 °C, for 1 minute and carefully discard all supernatant with a micropipette.
Dry the pellet at room temperature for 5 minutes (do not over-dry).

steps.title: Storage and Shipping
steps.instruction: Tag and seal tubes for shipment to a Proteomic Facility or store at -80 °C.

substeps.instruction: Store protein pellets from cytosol and gradient fractions at -80 °C.
If not using density gradients, store nuclear, mitochondrial, and microsomal pellets at -80 °C; otherwise, proceed to separation immediately.
